transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent, and I'm here to help you with any questions you might have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. To start, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but you can then go back to light exercise, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling. However, it's good to avoid strenuous, heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I also wanted to know when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Although it's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as it adjusts to the new lenses, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful, and we may need to assess this further. Otherwise, if it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for all the information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! So, just to confirm, all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again for your help!

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent successfully conveyed all three content points in a single turn. `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` was covered by "Although it's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as it adjusts to the new lenses". `escalation_criteria` was covered by "significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful, and we may need to assess this further." `mild_case_advice` was covered by "Otherwise, if it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside."
